activities.anchor: whether a defibrillator arrives while the heart's rhythm can still be shocked
activities.caption: bet before you read on — where survival is decided
activities.name: emsMinutePredict

config.q: In the ten minutes after a witnessed collapse, where is the biggest share of the survival outcome decided?
choices: In the ambulance's speed once the crew arrives
In what happens before any paramedic arrives — recognition, the call, bystander CPR, an early shock
In the receiving hospital's resuscitation room
In which drugs the crew carries
config.why: Outcomes are created by the whole chain connecting the collapse to definitive care — the crew, however excellent, arrives in the middle of the story, not at its start.

activities.anchor: In systems engineered for those early minutes
activities.caption: guess the magnitude — the engineered-system result
activities.name: emsSeattleEstimate

config.prompt: In systems engineered around the early links (Seattle and King County are the standard citation), survival from witnessed, shockable arrests has reached roughly…
config.why: Half or more — against a background where survival falls roughly 7–10 per cent for every minute without CPR and defibrillation, and bystander CPR can double or triple survival.
config.context: the difference is system design, not paramedic skill

activities.anchor: a "load and go to the right place" decision made before the wheels roll
activities.caption: pair each system part with its job
activities.name: emsPartsMatch

config.prompt: Inside the machine — pair each named part with its job:

pairs.right: universal emergency numbers and call-takers running scripted priority protocols
first responders beneath BLS ambulances beneath ALS paramedic units
a physician owns the clinical system — standing orders plus real-time consultation
route to the stroke centre or PCI-capable cath lab, not the nearest door

config.why: And the system runs on data: quality-assurance review of every arrest and protocol deviation — the loop that has repeatedly rewritten practice.

activities.anchor: facility rather than the nearest one
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the transport doctrine
activities.name: emsScoopSpot

config.prompt: One line of this doctrine brief is wrong — click it:
lines: Definitive care for time-critical conditions begins in the field — defibrillation, haemorrhage control, airway management.
The modern ideal: bring the emergency department to the patient.
Transport then goes to the nearest door — all emergency doors are interchangeable.
Even the siren is rationed: its time saving is small against the crash risk it multiplies.
The siren is treated as a clinical decision, like a drug with benefits and side effects.
config.correction: Transport goes to the right facility — trauma systems and cardiac and stroke networks route to capability, not proximity.
config.why: Continuity of care means capability-matched destination — 'scoop and run' is the misconception the evidence rejected.

activities.anchor: taught as career-length survival skills, not conveniences
activities.caption: file each hazard by its toll
activities.name: emsHazardSort

config.prompt: Protecting the protectors — file each hazard:

items.label: struck-by incidents — crews hit by traffic at highway scenes
musculoskeletal damage from lifting patients in stairwells and bathrooms
the reason stair chairs and powered stretchers exist at all

config.why: The statistics shape the training: the deadliest risks arrive at speed, the most common injury accumulates one lift at a time.

activities.anchor: waiting outside an unsafe scene is an act of patient care delivered indirectly
activities.caption: sequence the scene discipline
activities.name: emsSceneOrder

items: Survey for hazards before any patient contact — traffic, downed lines, fire, structural instability, hazmat placards
Park the ambulance angled across the roadway to block a lane; wear high-visibility apparel
Stage outside until police secure a violent scene — weapons are assumed present until cleared
Only then, patient contact — a dead or injured paramedic saves no one
config.why: Two patients help nobody — the discipline exists so that helping does not multiply the harm.

activities.caption: true or false — crew resource management
activities.name: emsCrmJudge

statements.s: Closed-loop instruction means repeating an order back so error is caught before it executes.
statements.why: One of the explicit-communication habits CRM installs.

statements.s: Most ambulance crashes and clinical errors trace to hurry, tunnel vision and unchallenged assumptions.
statements.why: Which is why shared situational awareness and the authority of any crew member to halt a deteriorating plan matter.

statements.s: Only the senior crew member may halt a deteriorating plan.
statements.why: Any crew member holds that authority — hierarchy does not outrank safety.

statements.s: Wellness teaching — stress first aid, peer support, fatigue management — is soft skill bolted onto a clinical course.
statements.why: It is what makes a twenty-year career of cardiac arrests and violence sustainable.

activities.anchor: the patient whose "refusal" is really hypoxia
activities.caption: walk the consent edge cases
activities.name: emsConsentBranch

config.root: Three consent edge cases, one discipline. Walk the law's answers.

start.text: An unconscious crash patient, no family present. On what basis does the crew treat?

choices.label: Implied consent — the law assumes a reasonable person would want resuscitation
The crew must wait for a guardian

wait.text: Capacity is absent and delay threatens life — implied consent exists for exactly this case.

implied.text: Next: a patient 'refuses' — slurring, barely oriented. Is that a refusal?

choices.label: No — a counterfeit of choice; incapacity, so implied consent applies
Yes — adults are presumed to have capacity

presumed.text: Capacity is presumed in adults but must be assessed — hypoxia, head injury and intoxication can all fake a choice.

masquerade.text: Last: a DNR order. It must be honoured — verified, never assumed from hearsay.

config.why: An informed refusal is as much a clinical act as an intubation — consent structures every contact, and capacity is the hinge.
